subject: Full Syllabus
summary: a mixed full-syllabus warm-up for the fifth full-length mock: instrument analogies, train-and-platform speed, inverse Laplace transforms, the trapezoidal rule, lifting-machine efficiency, shear in I-beams, shaft torsion, the steering-gear condition, natural frequency from static deflection, Petroff's bearing equation, hydraulic turbine power, composite walls, the Carnot refrigerator, non-consumable electrodes and pull production control

solution: Concept: The pair links an instrument to the quantity it measures.
A thermometer measures temperature. A barometer measures pressure, a hygrometer humidity and a rain gauge rainfall.
An anemometer measures wind speed, option (C).
Exam tip: State the relation in a short sentence ('X measures Y') and test each option in the same sentence.

questions.text: A train 180 m long crosses a platform 120 m long in 15 seconds. The speed of the train (in km/h) is ______
solution: Concept: To cross a platform the train must cover its own length plus the platform length.
Exam tip: Crossing a pole or a person needs only the train's own length; crossing a platform or bridge needs both lengths.

questions.text: The inverse Laplace transform of F(s) = 1/[s(s + 1)] is
solution: Concept: Split into partial fractions, then use L−1{1/s} = 1 and L−1{1/(s + a)} = e−at.
So f(t) = 1 − e−t, option (B).
Exam tip: Check with the initial value theorem: sF(s) → 0 as s → ∞, so f(0) = 0, which only 1 − e−t satisfies.

questions.text: The integral of x³ from x = 0 to x = 1 is evaluated by the trapezoidal rule with four equal strips (h = 0.25). The value obtained (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Trapezoidal rule: I ≈ (h/2)[y0 + 2(y1 + y2 + y3) + y4].
Exam tip: For a function that curves upward (convex), the trapezoidal rule always over-estimates the integral.

questions.text: In a lifting machine with a velocity ratio of 20, an effort of 50 N just lifts a load of 800 N. The efficiency of the machine (in %) is ______
solution: Concept: Efficiency = mechanical advantage ÷ velocity ratio, where MA = load/effort.
Exam tip: An ideal (frictionless) machine would lift VR × effort = 1000 N; the 'lost' 200 N of load is the effect of friction.

questions.text: The I-section beam shown carries a vertical shear force. Which statement about the transverse shear stress in the section is correct?
opts: It is greatest at the top and bottom fibres
It is uniform over the whole depth
The flanges carry most of the shear force
The web carries most of the shear force, and the stress is greatest at the neutral axis
questions.ans: (D) The web carries most of the shear force, and the stress is greatest at the neutral axis
solution: Concept: τ = VQ/(Ib): the shear stress depends on the first moment Q of the area beyond the level and on the width b at that level.
Q is zero at the top and bottom fibres and greatest at the neutral axis, so τ is greatest there.
Where the width drops from the flange width to the thin web, τ jumps up sharply; the web therefore carries most (typically 90–95 %) of the vertical shear: option (D).
Exam tip: For design, the web shear stress of an I-beam is often taken as V/(web depth × web thickness).

questions.text: A solid circular shaft of 40 mm diameter is subjected to a torque of 1 kN·m. The maximum shear stress in the shaft (in MPa, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: For a solid circular shaft, τmax = 16T/(πd3), at the outer surface.
T = 1 × 10<sup>6</sup> N·mm; d<sup>3</sup> = 64 000 mm³.
Exam tip: Keep N and mm together so the answer comes out directly in MPa (N/mm²).

questions.text: For correct steering (pure rolling of all four wheels about a common centre) of a car with wheelbase b and distance c between the front stub-axle pivots, the angles turned by the outer front wheel (φ) and the inner front wheel (θ) must satisfy
solution: Concept: All wheel axes must meet at one point (the instantaneous centre) on the line of the rear axle.
If that point is at distance x from the inner pivot along the rear axle line: cot θ = x/b and cot φ = (x + c)/b.
Subtracting: cot φ − cot θ = c/b, option (A). The outer wheel turns through the smaller angle.
Exam tip: The Davis gear satisfies this condition exactly at all angles; the Ackermann linkage satisfies it only at three positions, but is simpler (only turning pairs).

questions.text: A machine mounted on springs deflects them statically by 2.5 mm under its own weight. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the natural frequency of its vertical vibration (in Hz, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: mg = kδ gives k/m = g/δ, so fn = (1/2π)√(g/δ).
Exam tip: A handy shortcut is fn ≈ 15.76/√δ with δ in mm (here 15.76/1.581 = 9.97 Hz).

questions.text: Petroff's equation for the friction coefficient of a journal bearing applies to
opts: a heavily loaded bearing with a large eccentricity
a bearing working with boundary lubrication
a lightly loaded bearing in which the journal is taken as concentric with the bearing
questions.ans: (C) a lightly loaded bearing in which the journal is taken as concentric with the bearing
solution: Concept: Petroff assumed a full oil film of uniform thickness equal to the radial clearance c, i.e. zero eccentricity.
With a linear velocity profile the viscous shear gives f = 2π<sup>2</sup>(μN/p)(r/c).
This holds only for light loads at high speed, where the journal runs nearly concentric: option (C).
Exam tip: At heavier loads the journal moves off centre and the full hydrodynamic (Sommerfeld/Raimondi–Boyd) analysis is needed.

questions.text: A hydraulic turbine works under a net head of 100 m with a flow of 2 m³/s, and its overall efficiency is 90 %. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², its shaft power output (in MW, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Water power = ρgQH; shaft power = overall efficiency × water power.
Shaft power = 0.9 × 1.962 = 1.77 MW.
Exam tip: 1 m³/s falling through 1 m gives about 9.81 kW — a quick check on the order of magnitude.

questions.text: A composite wall has two layers of equal thickness in perfect contact, and the conductivity of layer 1 is twice that of layer 2. In steady one-dimensional conduction the total temperature drop across the wall is 90 °C. The temperature drop across layer 2 is
solution: Concept: In series the same heat flux passes through each layer, so each temperature drop is proportional to its thermal resistance L/k.
R<sub>2</sub> = L/k<sub>2</sub> and R<sub>1</sub> = L/(2k<sub>2</sub>) = R<sub>2</sub>/2, so ΔT<sub>2</sub> : ΔT<sub>1</sub> = 2 : 1.
ΔT2 = 90 × 2/3 = 60 °C, option (B).
Exam tip: The poorer conductor always takes the larger share of the temperature drop — the idea behind insulation.

questions.text: A Carnot refrigerator keeps a cold space at −23 °C while rejecting heat to surroundings at 27 °C. Its coefficient of performance is ______
solution: Concept: For a reversible refrigerator, COP = TL/(TH − TL), with absolute temperatures.
T<sub>L</sub> = 250 K, T<sub>H</sub> = 300 K.
Exam tip: Never use °C in this formula: 23/50 or −23/50 are the usual wrong answers.

questions.text: Which one of the following arc welding processes uses a non-consumable electrode?
solution: Concept: In a consumable-electrode process the electrode melts and becomes the filler metal.
SMAW (coated stick), SAW (bare wire under flux) and MIG (continuously fed wire) all melt their electrodes.
TIG uses a tungsten electrode that does not melt; filler, if needed, is added separately: option (D).
Exam tip: Plasma arc welding also uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode.

questions.text: Which one of the following is a 'pull' system of production control?
opts: Scheduling production in advance from a sales forecast
Releasing fixed economic batch quantities on a set calendar
solution: Concept: In a pull system, a downstream stage's actual consumption triggers production upstream; in a push system, production is released to a plan or forecast.
MRP, forecast-based scheduling and calendar batch release all push work into the shop.
Kanban cards authorise production only when parts are used: Kanban (JIT), option (A).
Exam tip: The number of kanbans N = D(Tw + Tp)(1 + α)/C caps the work-in-process.
